symptom: Menu rows continue from the previous cursor position, overflow the viewport, and wrap into displaced fragments on the left and right edges.
cause: The renderer used Console.SetCursorPosition and silently ignored host failures, so it kept writing after the preceding segment instead of starting each row at its declared coordinates.
violatedInvariant: Every menu row starts at its declared terminal coordinate independently of support for the .NET console cursor API.

must: Express cursor positions with the terminal-native ANSI cursor-position sequence.
Convert the layout's zero-based coordinates to ANSI's one-based row and column coordinates.
Leave redirected output free of cursor-control sequences.

automation.residual: Interactive rendering still requires the VT-compatible terminal already required by Deckle's alternate-screen and pointer-input controls.
